literal: To those who hide their wealth, where will hide, I wonder, the life of those who beg, which departs as they speak?
translation: When those who beg merely speak their need, their life departs from them out of shame. Where, then, does the life of those who hide their wealth go and hide?
modern: இரப்பவர்கள் தம் தேவையைச் சொல்லும்போதே அவமானம் தாங்காமல் அவர்களுடைய உயிர் போய்விடுகிறது; அப்படியிருக்க, இல்லை என்று ஒளித்து வைப்பவர்களுடைய உயிர் எங்கே போய் ஒளிந்து கொள்ளுமோ?
explanation: This couplet highlights the intense shame associated with begging and withholding. The poet observes that when a needy person merely utters a request for help, the sheer humiliation is so painful that their life-force (uyir) departs from them. If the act of asking is so fatal to the beggar's soul, the poet wonders where the soul of the hoarder (karappavar) goes to hide. Since refusing to give is a far more shameful act than begging, the hoarder's soul should logically flee in even greater disgrace, yet they continue to live unaffected.
